record.original_question: Let p_n be the probability that the zero solution of the random nth-order linear differential equation A_n x^(n) + ... + A_0 x = 0, with i.i.d. N(0,1) coefficients, is globally asymptotically stable. Determine the asymptotic expansion of p_n as n tends to infinity and decide whether the sequence p_n is strictly decreasing.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let pn be the probability that the zero solution of the n-th order linear random differential equation (18) is globally asymptotically stable. Find the asymptotic expansion of pn at n = infinity. Is it true that the sequence pn is strictly decreasing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A_0, A_1, \dots, A_n$ be independent identically distributed standard normal random variables, and consider the random $n$-th order linear homogeneous differential equation
$$A_n x^{(n)}(t) + A_{n-1} x^{(n-1)}(t) + \cdots + A_1 x'(t) + A_0 x(t) = 0.$$
The zero solution of this equation is said to be globally asymptotically stable if every solution $x(t)$ tends to $0$ as $t \to \infty$; equivalently, the (random) characteristic polynomial $A_n z^n + A_{n-1} z^{n-1} + \cdots + A_0$ is a Hurwitz polynomial (i.e., all of its complex roots have strictly negative real part). Let
$$p_n = \mathbb{P}\bigl(\text{the zero solution of the above equation is globally asymptotically stable}\bigr).$$

(a) Determine a complete asymptotic expansion of $p_n$ as $n \to \infty$.

(b) Decide whether the sequence $(p_n)_{n \ge 1}$ is strictly decreasing.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found for the asymptotic expansion of $p_n$ or for the strict monotonicity of the sequence $p_n$ for random Hurwitz-stability probabilities of Gaussian-coefficient linear ODEs. The question appears in problem lists on random polynomials and remains open as far as the available literature on Hurwitz stability of random polynomials indicates.

status_evidence.title: Hurwitz polynomial - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A Hurwitz polynomial is one whose roots all have strictly negative real part; equivalently, the linear system is asymptotically stable.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the equivalence used in the problem between asymptotic stability and Hurwitz stability of the characteristic polynomial.

status_evidence.title: Routh–Hurwitz stability criterion - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Tests whether all roots of a polynomial lie in the open left half-plane.
status_evidence.claim: Standard background; no result on probabilistic asymptotics of $p_n$ for Gaussian-coefficient polynomials is reported.
